prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2001 – Summary

Core purpose and independence
- SNP stands for Scotland’s independence and putting Scotland’s interests first at Westminster.
- More SNP MPs strengthen the case for a referendum; a majority would trigger one.
- Seek immediate transfer of further powers to Holyrood and oppose anti-Scottish measures.

Fiscal strategy and investment
- Scotland is a wealthy country sending a surplus to Westminster.
- Create a Scottish Fund for Future Generations using oil revenues to deliver a permanent income stream.
- Create a Scottish Trust for Public Investment (STPI) to replace costly PFI/PPP and halve capital costs, unlocking large-scale infrastructure for health, education, housing and transport.

Constitution and governance
- Written constitution; inclusive citizenship; retain the Queen subject to referendum.
- Proportional representation at all levels; reform/abolish excessive quangos; opportunities for civil servants.

Education
- Abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance grants as resources allow.
- Establish an Education Convention; reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18; end league tables; cut assessment burdens.
- Major school refurbishment via STPI; implement McCrone; strengthen Gaelic medium, inclusion, and Scottish studies.

Economy, jobs and work
- Targeted infrastructure, broadband, and smarter enterprise agencies; integrate tourism into the enterprise network.
- Devolve/refocus New Deal into a Better Deal for job black spots and reskilling.
- Raise minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages; plan further rise; support small firms via tax reform.
- Statutory Charter of Trade Union Rights; support EU employee protections.

Environment, energy, water
- Climate strategy with State of the Nation audit and National Environment Plan.
- 12% of all energy (25% of electricity) from renewables by 2010; no new nuclear; lead on decommissioning.
- Expand recycling/resource efficiency; give SEPA powers over MoD.
- Review water charges; halt backdoor privatisation; democratise water bodies.

Health and care
- Create a National Health Care Commission; end postcode treatment with binding HTBS decisions.
- Free fruit for primary pupils; nutritional standards for school meals.
- Free dental check-ups; freeze and review prescription charges.
- Invest in equipment and cleanliness; recruit 1,500 nurses; aim to halve inpatient waiting times.
- Free personal care for all elderly people in need.

Europe, international, defence
- Pro-EU but oppose a superstate; stronger subsidiarity; euro only by referendum when conditions suit.
- As an independent state: full MEP quota, Council votes and a Commissioner.
- Remove Trident; oppose US missile defence; negotiate phased withdrawal from NATO while maintaining cooperation; form a Scottish Defence Force.
- Business-focused external offices; meet UN aid target; cancel Third World debt.

Culture, media, sport, languages
- Devolve broadcasting oversight; more powers/budget for BBC Scotland and a “Scottish Six”; support digital rollout.
- Focus sports funds on communities; football academies; bid for Euro 2008.
- Reform Arts Council; national theatre; Scottish Lottery for good causes.
- Secure status for Gaelic; promote Scots language.

Social justice, housing, equality
- National anti-poverty strategy and “poverty proofing”; humane asylum policy and end vouchers.
- Invest in housing via STPI; oppose wholesale stock transfer; devolve housing benefit.
- Core funding and water-charge exemption for voluntary sector; tackle homelessness.
- Enshrine equal opportunities; strengthen Disability Discrimination Act; drugs courts and treatment.

Crime and policing
- Fund 1,000 extra police officers; parental compensation orders for youth damage; lifelong restriction orders for high-risk sex offenders; faster courts; Sentencing Advisory Panel.

Tax and local government
- No rise in overall tax burden without mandate; comprehensive tax review for fairness/simplicity.
- Immediate 10p/gal fuel duty cut funded by a 5p income tax band over £100k.
- Review local government finance; explore local income tax; PR (STV) for councils.

Rural, agriculture, fisheries, land
- Cut fuel duty; improve rural transport and ICT; small business rates relief; protect key services; crisis contingency funds.
- Post–foot and mouth agriculture review; fair EU implementation; promote organics/diversification; ameliorate LFA.
- Fisheries: compensated tie-ups, conservation, devolved CFP via Zonal Councils; return 6,000 sq miles; salmon farming inquiry.
- Community land rights; national freshwater fisheries policy.

Pensions and welfare
- Restore earnings link for the basic state pension; pay winter fuel weekly; examine tax impacts on small pensions; aim to align pension with MIG.
- Streamline social security into a single agency; simplify benefits, including disability and housing benefit; extend winter fuel to severely disabled; review support for 16–17s and WFTC.

Transport
- Use STPI for rail reopenings, airport links and electrification (e.g., ECML, Borders line); concessionary fares for youth, students, pensioners and disabled people; explore light rail.
- Road repair plus targeted projects (e.g., M74, A75, Aberdeen bypass).
- Reduce ferry fares via Road Equivalent Tariff; abolish Skye Bridge tolls; strengthen airports and direct flights.
